methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Dual Component (Math + ELA)
content: Problem: In Phase 2, students must learn both hard academic concepts (Math / Place Value) and the language to explain them (ELA), which can cause cognitive overload if taught simultaneously.

Solution: Every session is strictly split. Part 1 (Math Component, 40 mins) focuses purely on reading big numbers, counting zeroes, and understanding digit positions. Part 2 (ELA Component, 80 mins) shifts to the grammatical structures needed to articulate these numbers clearly in English sentences.

parts.title: PART 1: MATH COMPONENT
content: A. Math Reading Input: The Bank Vault
Detective Max finds a secret bank vault (hầm chứa). It is a huge metal door. Max needs to find the code.
"The password (mật khẩu) is a big number," says Max. "I must understand the digits (chữ số)."
Max looks at his notes. "The number 100 is one hundred. It has three digits. One, zero, and another zero."
Max thinks. "If I add one more zero, the number gets bigger! The number 1,000 is one thousand. It has exactly four digits."
By counting the digits and the zeroes, Max can crack the code!

→ Memory trick: T-H-O: Three Huge zeroes

content: A. Math Reading Input: Pip's Winter Counting
Pip the squirrel has a lot of nuts for winter. He needs to understand large numbers.
Max helps him. "Every digit has a place (hàng / vị trí). In the number 5,000, the 5 is in the thousands place. The other digits are zeroes."
Max explains place value (giá trị). "The position (vị trí) of the digit is very important. If we move the 5 to the hundreds place, the number is 500. The value is completely different!"
Pip learns that changing the position changes the value!

Using sentences with "is in the [blank] place" helps detectives explain big numbers to anyone. Pip counts his 5,000 nuts perfectly without any mistakes!
